title: Forced-colours and contrast preferences
learningObjectives: Explain forced-colours and contrast preferences and create motion that respects user preferences.

understand.concept: The forced-colors media feature detects when the user agent enforces a limited colour palette, often to support accessibility settings. forced-color-adjust controls whether an element follows those forced colours. Contrast preference media features are support-dependent and should be treated progressively.
understand.whyItMatters: Do not override user-selected high-contrast colours for decorative consistency. Preserve system colours for text, borders, and controls unless there is a compelling, tested reason to opt out.
understand.analogy: Forced-colours mode is like a user-selected high-visibility palette that the page should respect rather than fight.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual animation, rendering, and preference handling follow CSS and browser behaviour.

explain.narrative: In forced-colours mode the control uses system colour keywords so its boundary and text remain visible.

examples.explanation: In forced-colours mode the control uses system colour keywords so its boundary and text remain visible.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the animation or user-preference behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Test a custom button in forced-colors mode. Remove unnecessary hard-coded colours and verify the focus indicator remains visible.
practise.independentTask: Build a small motion-enhanced component. Provide a static or reduced-motion state and test the result with keyboard interaction.
hints: Keep essential content visible without animation.
Test light/dark and forced-colours preferences where relevant.
Measure performance on a representative device.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Forced-colours and contrast preferences</title></head><body>
<button class='action'>Submit</button><style>.action{border:2px solid #245b48;padding:.8rem;background:#e8f1f8;color:#17324d}@media(forced-colors:active){.action{border:1px solid ButtonText;background:ButtonFace;color:ButtonText}}</style>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which media feature detects an active forced-colours mode?
questions.explanation: forced-colors:active indicates that the user agent is enforcing a limited palette.

questions.prompt: What should happen when a user requests reduced motion?
options: Non-essential movement should be removed or simplified
questions.answer: Non-essential movement should be removed or simplified
questions.explanation: The interface should preserve content and operation while respecting the preference.
